paper.title_en: Sign of quadrupole deformation dictates pseudospin symmetry breaking in resonant states
paper.abstract_en: Pseudospin symmetry (PSS) is a relativistic symmetry of the Dirac Hamiltonian that is strictly conserved for single-particle resonant states in spherical nuclei when <math altimg="si27.svg"><mrow><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Σ</mi></mstyle><mo>≡</mo><mi>S</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">+</mo><mi>V</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, but whether this strict conservation persists in deformed nuclei, and how the sign of quadrupole deformation affects PSS breaking, remain open questions. This work aims to systematically investigate the conservation and breaking mechanisms of PSS for single-particle resonant states in both spherical and axially deformed nuclei, with special emphasis on the asymmetric role of the deformation sign—a dimension not explored in previous studies. The complex momentum representation (CMR) method is adopted, extended to quadrupole-deformed Woods-Saxon potentials, providing a unified description of bound states, resonances, and the continuum, and enabling the calculation of energies, widths, and Dirac wavefunction components in both coordinate and momentum spaces. In spherical nuclei at <math altimg="si1.svg"><mrow><msub><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Σ</mi></mstyle><mn>0</mn></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, pseudospin partners have exactly the same energies, widths, and lower-component density distributions—strict conservation. In deformed nuclei, even at <math altimg="si1.svg"><mrow><msub><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Σ</mi></mstyle><mn>0</mn></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, deformation lifts degeneracy; PSS becomes only approximately conserved, with a clear asymmetry: prolate (β2 > 0) deformation yields small, stable splittings, while oblate (β2 < 0) deformation induces larger, more sensitive splittings. For fixed <math altimg="si12.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0.34</mn></mrow></math>, deepening the potential well increases splitting and drives resonances toward bound states, but does not alter the shape of density distributions. This work reveals, for the first time, that the sign of quadrupole deformation plays a crucial and asymmetric role in PSS breaking in resonant states—a dimension previously unexplored, providing a theoretical basis for understanding continuum coupling effects and exotic structures in weakly bound deformed nuclei.
